verses.english: Linked Discourses 7.14
2. Lay Followers
A well-to-do brahmin
At Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: Atha kho aññataro brāhmaṇamahāsālo lūkho lūkhapāvuraṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
verses.english: Then a certain well-to-do brahmin, shabby, wearing a shabby cloak, went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

verses.pali: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho taṁ brāhmaṇamahāsālaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
verses.english: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,
“Brahmin, why are you so shabby, wearing a shabby cloak?”
“Worthy Gotama, I have four sons.

verses.pali: Te maṁ dārehi sampuccha gharā nikkhāmentī”ti.
verses.english: At their wives’ bidding they expelled me from my house.”

verses.pali: “Tena hi tvaṁ, brāhmaṇa, imā gāthāyo pariyāpuṇitvā sabhāyaṁ mahājanakāye sannipatite puttesu ca sannisinnesu bhāsassu:
verses.english: “Well then, brahmin, memorize these verses and recite them to your sons when you are all seated in the council hall with a large crowd.
‘I was overjoyed when they were born,
and wished prosperity for them.
But at their wives’ bidding they chased me out,
like hounds after hogs.
It turns out they’re wicked, those nasty men,
though they called me their dear old Dad.
They’re monsters in the shape of sons,
throwing me out as I’ve grown old.
Like an old, useless horse
led away from its fodder,
the elderly father of those kids
begs for alms at others’ homes.
Even my staff is better
than those disobedient sons,
for it wards off a wild bull,
and even a wild dog.
It goes before me in the dark;
in deep waters it finds a footing.
By the wonderful power of this staff,
when I stumble, I stand firm again.’”

verses.pali: Atha kho so brāhmaṇamahāsālo bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo pariyāpuṇitvā sabhāyaṁ mahājanakāye sannipatite puttesu ca sannisinnesu abhāsi:
verses.english: Having memorized those verses in the Buddha’s presence, the brahmin recited them to his sons when they were all seated in the council hall with a large crowd. …

verses.pali: Atha kho naṁ brāhmaṇamahāsālaṁ puttā gharaṁ netvā nhāpetvā paccekaṁ dussayugena acchādesuṁ.
verses.english: Then the brahmin’s sons led him back home, bathed him, and each clothed him with a fine pair of garments.

verses.pali: Atha kho so brāhmaṇamahāsālo ekaṁ dussayugaṁ ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
verses.english: Then the brahmin, taking one pair of garments, went to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

verses.pali: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho brāhmaṇamahāsālo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

verses.pali: “mayaṁ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā nāma ācariyassa ācariyadhanaṁ pariyesāma.
verses.english: “Worthy Gotama, we brahmins seek a fee for our tutor.
May the worthy Gotama please accept my tutor’s fee!”
So the Buddha accepted it out of sympathy.

verses.pali: Atha kho so brāhmaṇamahāsālo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then the well-to-do brahmin said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama …

verses.pali: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
verses.english: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
